authoritativeSources.title: Zero Trust deployment approach with Microsoft Intune
Update your workloads to support cloud-native endpoints

recommendations.title: Review identity foundation and target cloud identity path
recommendations.purpose: Confirm the intended Microsoft Entra registration or join outcome before changing provisioning, enrollment, or access policy.
recommendations.priorityExplanation: Cloud identity targeting comes first because later management and access controls depend on it.
prerequisites: Confirm that the Assessment User Context and local registration evidence are complete.
Resolve tenant-side decisions about the intended join or enrollment path.
recommendations.caution: One endpoint cannot prove tenant assignment, licensing, compliance, or organization intent.
recommendations.verification: Validate the approved target state in the authorized Microsoft Entra and Intune administration boundaries before device reprovisioning.

recommendations.title: Review enrollment connectivity, DNS, and trust prerequisites
recommendations.purpose: Confirm that device-enrollment and identity endpoints can be reached through the approved DNS, proxy, TLS, and certificate path.
recommendations.priorityExplanation: Enrollment and access flows fail early when network or trust prerequisites are unresolved.
prerequisites: Approve and interpret the bounded connectivity and certificate evidence together.
Confirm tenant-specific DNS and proxy requirements in an authorized boundary.
recommendations.caution: Generic Microsoft endpoint success does not prove tenant-specific enrollment DNS, authorization, or future service health.
recommendations.verification: Compare the protected evidence with the approved enterprise proxy, DNS, TLS-interception, and certificate design before rollout.

recommendations.title: Plan application, resource, and privilege dependency transition
recommendations.purpose: Review local software, resource, peripheral, and administrator dependencies before applying a new management or access model.
recommendations.priorityExplanation: Dependency review should happen before compliant-device enforcement so critical business access is not guessed.
prerequisites: Confirm which local dependencies must be retained, replaced, or retired.
Validate approved support information for retained applications and peripherals.
recommendations.caution: Observed inventory and membership do not prove compatibility, support, approval, or least-privilege readiness.
recommendations.verification: Map retained dependencies to the target build, packaging, access, and support model before cutover.

recommendations.title: Plan policy and security-control modernization
recommendations.purpose: Translate the validated local policy and security-control state into an approved cloud management and security baseline plan.
recommendations.priorityExplanation: Modern policy translation should happen after identity and connectivity are understood but before compliant-device enforcement is tightened.
prerequisites: Separate Applied Policy Evidence, Configured Policy Signals, and Current Control State.
Resolve unsupported, denied, stale, or contradictory policy evidence before claiming a target baseline.
recommendations.caution: One endpoint cannot prove tenant assignment, universal precedence, organization-wide scope, or service-side compliance.
recommendations.verification: Map the protected local evidence to the approved Intune, Conditional Access, and security-baseline design without assuming direct one-to-one policy equivalence.

recommendations.title: Stage compliant-device access, device risk, and advanced data protection
recommendations.purpose: Move from validated local readiness into approved compliant-device access, device-risk integration, and advanced endpoint data-protection rollout only after prerequisite path steps are understood.
recommendations.priorityExplanation: These controls come after identity, connectivity, dependency, and policy groundwork because they depend on a stable managed-device baseline.
prerequisites: Confirm the cloud identity target state and enrollment path.
Resolve material dependency and policy-translation blockers.
Confirm tenant-side Conditional Access, compliance, and security-operations scope.
recommendations.caution: WIN-PCInfo does not produce a fixed rollout schedule, a compliance verdict, or an automatic remediation plan.
recommendations.verification: Validate that managed-device enrollment, compliance policies, and approved access controls are ready before expanding to device-risk and endpoint DLP stages.

discoveryTasks.purpose: Confirm the tenant-side Conditional Access, compliance, and approved protection tier target for this device class.
discoveryTasks.expectedSafeResult: A documented target access tier and compliant-device requirement decision without exporting tenant identifiers or policy values.

discoveryTasks.purpose: Confirm whether Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, device risk, and endpoint data protection are in scope for the approved migration phase.
discoveryTasks.expectedSafeResult: An approved in-scope, later-phase, or unavailable conclusion without fabricating service-side onboarding state.

discoveryTasks.purpose: Confirm the tenant-specific enrollment DNS, proxy, and certificate-path requirements that cannot be proven from one endpoint alone.
discoveryTasks.expectedSafeResult: A confirmed, blocked, or unresolved tenant-specific enrollment path conclusion without exporting tenant DNS labels or private certificate material.

relationships.explanation: A stable identity target makes policy translation and assignment planning meaningful.
Compliant-device access depends on a reachable and trusted management plane.
Unresolved legacy dependencies can conflict with immediately requiring a new managed-device access model.
Approved policy translation and assignment planning enable compliant-device and device-risk stages.
